subject.title: [Bug]: OpenAI-compatible streaming tool calls are dropped when provider omits finish_reason

question: Should OpenClaw execute native streamed tool calls when an OpenAI-compatible provider emits valid `delta.tool_calls` and a clean raw SSE `[DONE]` terminator but no final `finish_reason`?
rationale: This changes the provider-output-to-tool-execution boundary, and current code intentionally fails closed for missing-finish streams to avoid executing tool calls from truncated output.

options.title: Accept clean-DONE promotion
options.body: Land the linked PR if maintainers accept native tool-call deltas plus raw SSE `[DONE]` as a clean terminal signal while keeping EOF-without-DONE fail-closed.

options.title: Require exact-provider proof
options.body: Ask for one redacted Evolink or equivalent live provider run before accepting the widened execution contract.

options.title: Keep finish_reason required
options.body: Close or reject the linked fix path if maintainers decide explicit `finish_reason` remains mandatory for streamed tool execution.

recommendation.title: Accept clean-DONE promotion
recommendation.body: Land the linked PR if maintainers accept native tool-call deltas plus raw SSE `[DONE]` as a clean terminal signal while keeping EOF-without-DONE fail-closed.

likelyOwner.reason: Reviewed and merged the prior stop-finished tool-call guard and is the clearest routing owner for accepting or rejecting the adjusted execution boundary.
